evidence: STRUCTURE (source-level, passes): tests/scoring.toml and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean): gates render=0.0/constraints=0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05. score.py:57-59 reward = sum(w*score)/sum(w) only if every gate > 0 and functional > 0.05, else 0.0; scores are validated finite in [0,1] (score.py:24-31). Every term is non-negative and each gate/floor is a non-decreasing step, so reward is non-decreasing in every criterion score: an app that satisfies a superset of criteria can never score lower. Gates (all_pass, binary, weight 1.0) carry no mass and test only a minimal shared-storage create/readback and wrong-vs-right password sign-in (gates/constraints/judge.toml hro_gate_shared, gates/render/judge.toml hro_gate_render) - behaviours any stronger app also has, so no gate is failed by a stronger app. Mass: functional 44 binary rows, weights sum 59.5 (0.5-2.5); polish 5 binary rows sum 12; visual 5 Likert(5) rows x1.2. Functional 0.6 > craft; true craft (visual) is 0.2, and polish rows are concurrency behaviours (live-update preservation, paged-place, failed send, session drafts) named in instruction.md lines 5,7 and hireops_rules.md sec 5-6, so craft does not outweigh function. CRITERION-LEVEL MONOTONICITY (weak app must not pass by doing nothing): polish hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread state 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds, preservation cannot be shown and this row is 0' (so a non-live app cannot trivially 'preserve' drafts and outscore a live one); every refusal row names a same-kind positive control (hro_interview_full, hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_mgr_other_job, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places, hro_undo_conflict, hro_undo_once, hro_activity_refusals, hro_pol_failed_send, hro_pol_session_resume), and functional prompt.md line 13 requires 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'; hro_candidate_private and hro_candidate_no_staff give 0 when the candidate receives none of their own data. CONFORMING ALTERNATIVES NOT PENALISED: hiding disallowed controls is optional with server replay graded instead (functional prompt.md line 23; hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_hired, hro_observer_readonly); hro_refused_put_back also passes a UI that refuses before moving; replays first fetch current version so only the rule under test can refuse (prompt.md line 17); status codes demanded by hro_anonymous/hro_refusal_status (401/403/404/409) are public in hireops_rules.md lines 21-23 and 77-80. Scored-dimension in-prompt gates (functional prompt.md 11-13, polish 66-67, visual 86-87) mirror the constraints gate and floor to 0 / Likert 1 consistently. Attempted counterexamples: (1) dead or static app -> fails constraints gate -> 0; (2) app with no live updates but perfect drafts -> loses hro_live_board, hro_unread_* and both polish live rows -> lower than a live app; (3) app without stale-version checks -> hro_stale_refused 0; (4) app showing all 120 messages (no paging) -> hro_thread_latest/hro_thread_earlier/hro_pol_earlier_place 0. None inverts. NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS: (a) a single visual Likert row spans 0.04 of reward and the heaviest polish row 0.05, while the heaviest functional row is 2.5/59.5*0.6 = 0.025, so trade-offs (e.g. a privacy leak in hro_candidate_private vs illegible typography) can favour the prettier app; this is a weighting-honesty trade-off (row 44), not a dominance inversion. (b) The functional floor makes a cliff at 0.05 by template design (not task-editable). RISK (why risk=true): raw-evidence-index.json scope says verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' REVIEW_POLICY.md requires hash-bound reward-ordering records from mutated weak apps before clearance; none exist. Also unmeasured: functional judge timeout = 9000 s inside scored suite budget 11100 s (test.sh:224) run sequentially with polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 s; if a fuller, better app drives the 44-row protocol past 9000 s, the scored suite fails and test.sh:224-227 writes reward 0 while a weaker app that short-circuits could finish and score >0 - a possible budget-driven ranking inversion that only a full configured judge run can rule in or out. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
